brief: 8 Claude Code patterns that separate hobbyists from operators — concrete examples each.

slots.body: Six patterns that turn weekend experiments into production-grade operator workflows. No theory—just concrete tactics you can deploy today.
Operators define Pydantic models before writing prompts. Hobbyists free-type and pray the JSON parses.
slots.card1Body: API integrations, batch extraction, and any pipeline where downstream code expects typed data.
slots.card2Body: The model performs better when it sees the empty JSON skeleton in the system prompt.

slots.body: Generate, score, and rewrite in the same turn. A critic agent catches hallucinations before they reach the user.
slots.card1Body: Long-form content, code review, and safety-critical outputs that need high correctness.
slots.card2Body: A 3-line rubric in the critic prompt beats a 50-line instruction in the generator prompt.

slots.body: Operators count tokens like dollars. They tier memory: system, few-shot, retrieved, and ephemeral scratchpad.
slots.card1Body: Multi-turn support, large document QA, and keeping latency low under token pressure.
slots.card2Body: Moving examples from system to dynamic retrieval cuts input tokens by 40% without losing accuracy.

slots.body: Every operator pipeline ends with a validation layer. Regex, type checks, and a second pass for policy violations.
slots.card1Body: Customer-facing bots, automated PR reviewers, and any agent with write access to production.
slots.card2Body: Fail loudly with a structured error object instead of silently returning malformed data.

slots.body: Hobbyists describe tools in prose. Operators write OpenAPI-style specs and let the model reason about dependencies.
slots.card1Body: Calculators, search, code interpreters, and any workflow requiring external state changes.
slots.card2Body: Adding a thinking parameter to the tool schema forces the model to show its work before acting.

slots.body: Specialized agents own single domains. A router delegates, collects context, and never lets context bleed between tasks.
slots.card1Body: Customer support triage, research pipelines, and complex workflows with conflicting tool sets.
slots.card2Body: State machines beat chat history. Pass a structured payload, not a wall of text, between agents.

slots.body: Deploy one pattern today and measure the before-and-after quality shift.
slots.quote: Operators ship systems. Hobbyists ship prompts.
